correctness.rationale: Projection terms reduce to a single variable. In the nonprojection case, a noninvertible B=1−T gives the strict intermediate probability |ker B|/|A| for x*y=y. When B and T are invertible their inverses belong to the finite ring R=Z[T]=Z[B] by finite order. On the finite set of realized binary coefficients, the maps f↦Bf and f↦Bf+T are permutations. Composing the second with the inverse of the first and conjugating by powers of the first yields translations by B^jT. Their additive span is TR=R; starting with coefficient zero gives all of R without adding operations to the term language. A nonzero nonunit of R acts nontrivially but nonbijectively (a bijective endomorphism has a positive power equal to the identity), and so gives a two-variable strict intermediate probability. Conversely, if R is a field, any equation with a nonzero difference coefficient defines an onto linear map onto A and has exactly probability 1/|A|. A field R acts on A as a finite vector space and T generates it with scalar distinct from 0 and 1. For B invertible the displacement group acts by all additive translations: conjugating it forces an isomorphism fixing zero to be additive, then to intertwine T. Rational canonical form gives one class per allowed irreducible polynomial and centralizer GL_{m/d}(F_{p^d}); multiplying by the translation factor and using relabeling gives the stated formulas and the unique projection operation. Independently closed the actual binary operation truth vectors on (x,0) over ten small abelian groups and tested order-four and order-nine stabilizers on their tables; the order-nine nonprojection class orbit sizes were 840, 5040, 5040 and 5040, totaling 15960 before the projection.

originality.rationale: The earlier October 26 catalogue result already classifies the full spectrum of finite Latin affine quandles on elementary abelian groups. In particular it gives precisely the field/irreducible-minimal-polynomial criterion, explicitly allows multiplicity greater than one, and gives binary witnesses; this is established earlier coverage, not a speculative match. Cardó's more general theorem already forces Latinness of a nonprojection idempotent minimal-spectrum groupoid. The frozen proof correctly extends the coefficient argument to nonelementary groups and gives exact filtered counts, but those do not substantiate the principal classification as a distinct finding. The nonelementary exclusion reduces to an integer multiplier once the same finite ring-generation argument is applied, and the counts are routine consequences of the earlier positive cases, known affine-quandle isomorphism theory and orbit–stabilizer. No claim is made that the exact count formulas were located verbatim.
residual_risks: Hou 2012 and the inaccessible listed sources were not read as full text; precise printed-formula priority for the counts is unresolved.
The failure rests on the affirmative earlier classification and concrete implications, not on access limitations or any claim that every part appeared verbatim.

value.rationale: Minimal-spectrum classification is a natural question, and the frozen formulas are correct. But after crediting the earlier full Latin spectrum, the additional nonelementary exclusion is a direct prime-multiplier test, and counting the already determined positive class is irreducible-polynomial counting plus a standard centralizer and relabeling calculation. The record does not establish a separate nonroutine invariant, witness phenomenon or application in that remainder. No scientifically distinct repair is delivered.
residual_risks: This does not rule out value in a stronger full spectral classification on nonelementary finite abelian groups; that claim is outside this record.
